conventions.unverified: The literal string 'unverified' means the value was not found in a published source. Nothing was guessed, averaged, or converted from SI to fill a gap. Where only SI values exist they are quoted as printed in a note and the inch-pound field stays 'unverified'.
conventions.src: Every fact carries 'src', a list of ids in that material's own 'sources' array. Source ids are P1, P2, ... and are scoped to the material. Each source has its exact URL, publication number or date, access date and retrieval method.
conventions.products: Values are per product and never merged. Where two products differ, both are given and the difference is listed in 'discrepancies_between_products'.
conventions.typical_values: Manufacturer data sheets report typical or average values subject to manufacturing variation and change without notice. Confirm against the current sheet before using a number in a submittal.
conventions.quote: 'quote' fields hold text copied verbatim from the cited source (pdftotext or rendered-page reading; several excerpts are joined with ' | '). Typographic marks may differ where pdftotext rendered them differently; this is noted where it matters.

method: Manufacturer PDFs were downloaded and read from their raw text (pdftotext). Where a table was an image, the rendered page was read instead; this is noted on that source's 'retrieval'. ASTM scope text comes from the public astm.org store pages, since full ASTM tables are paywalled. Same structure as materials-verified.json; per-product 'sizes' adds 'form' (half-shell, blanket wrapped in layers, tube) and 'multi_layer' (published single-layer limits or layering rules).
product_availability_notes: Polyisocyanurate: Trymer 2000XP is a current Johns Manville product (JM announced its acquisition of ITW Insulation Systems, a 'low-temperature polyisocyanurate' maker, on 2019-11-21). Dyplast Products 'has joined the North American region of Kingspan's Insulation Division' (archived dyplastproducts.com, 2025) and its site is now offline. Kingspan US sells Tarecpir (2.0–6.0 pcf; pipe form Tarecpir 360), and the Tarecpir 2.0 property table matches the archived ISO-C1/2.0 table line for line, but no document states the rename, so ISO-C1 = Tarecpir 2.0 is an inference. Dyplast ISO-C1 is therefore not populated separately.

Aerogel: Aspen Aerogels Pyrogel XTE (data sheet Rev 4.2) and Cryogel Z (Rev 9.0) are populated; Aspen lists both sheets for the United States region. Aspen's current install manuals sit behind a contact form, so layer, vapor-barrier and jacketing rules come from Aspen-authored copies hosted by distributors (Pyrogel XTE/XTF manual VER 6.2, 2017; Cryogel cold-service manual Rev 1.2). Armacell ArmaGel HT/HTL/DT is not populated: no US-market data sheet with inch-pound values was found (armacell.com en-US returned HTTP 403; only regional TDSs such as en-VN/ID/PH/SG were located).

Expanded perlite: JM Sproule WR-1200 (formerly Industrial Insulation Group) data are from its April 2025 sheets, but on 2026-10-11 its jm.com product page redirected away and it was missing from JM's 2025–26 industrial selector guides, so whether it is still sold is unconfirmed. Other US-sold C610 pipe products recorded: Howred GOODTEMP (undated sheet, PDF 2005, numeric k), SMC Industries AU-1200 (Houston, April 2025, k as a graph only) and imported TPS EP-12 (2022, k as a graph only). SMC and TPS therefore have no k points.

Polyolefin: Armacell ArmaLight Tubolit (Americas TDS 102024 en-US, Oct 2024) and K-FLEX USA K-FLEX PE (US_LEA_PE_V3_0523) are both current US C1427 Type I tubes, 3/8–1 in wall, 6 ft, rated to 200°F, aimed at residential and light commercial work. Armacell's own armacell.com copy of the Tubolit TDS was blocked by a bot check, so a distributor-hosted Armacell PDF was used; a possible newer 'TDS 062026' edition was seen in search results but not read. Nomaco and IMCOA polyolefin products were not reviewed.

astm_spec.designation: ASTM C591-22 (Active per ASTM store page; prior editions C591-21, C591-20, C591-19a, C591-19, C591-17 ...)
astm_spec.title: Standard Specification for Unfaced Preformed Rigid Cellular Polyisocyanurate Thermal Insulation
astm_spec.scope_summary: Abstract: covers 'unfaced, preformed rigid cellular polyurethane modified polyisocyanurate plastic material intended for use as thermal insulation on surfaces'; 'can be classified into six types according to its compressive resistance: Types I, IV, II, III, V, and VI' and 'as Grades 1 and 2 according to its service temperature range'. Required properties: density, compressive resistance, apparent thermal conductivity, hot-surface performance, water absorption, water vapor permeability, dimensional stability, closed-cell content, surface burning characteristics, tensile strength, leachable chloride/fluoride/silicate/sodium. 1.1: 'intended for use as thermal insulation on surfaces from –297°F (–183°C) to 300°F (149°C). For specific applications, the actual temperature limits shall be agreed upon by the manufacturer and purchaser.' 1.3: 'designed as a material specification, not a design document ... Below –70°F (–51°C) the manufacturer and the purchaser must agree on what additional cold temperature performance properties are required'. 1.4: ODP-0 blowing agents only. 1.5: except clauses on size/shape and storage of fabricated parts, 'the requirements in this standard specification apply to the polyisocyanurate insulation in the form of buns supplied by the insulation manufacturer.' Numeric type/grade limits are in the paywalled standard and are not reproduced on the scope page.

types_grades.note: Lowest compressive-resistance type in the C591 ordering 'Types I, IV, II, III, V, and VI'. Example: JM Trymer 1800 (1.8 lb PCF) 'ASTM C591, Grade 2, Type I Complies'. Numeric Type I limits not on the public page (unverified). max_use_temp_f is the C591 scope limit.

2.0 pcf class. JM Trymer 2000XP: 'ASTM C591, Grade 2, Type IV Complies'; Kingspan Tarecpir 2.0: 'Meets ASTM C591 Type IV classification'. Type IV limits as reproduced in Kingspan's 'ASTM C591 Max or Min' column (manufacturer reproduction of C591 Section 12, not checked against the paywalled standard): density ≥2.0 (32) pcf; compressive parallel ≥22 (150) psi; apparent k (C177, aged) ≤0.13 @ -200°F, ≤0.15 @ -150°F, ≤0.17 @ -100°F, ≤0.19 @ -50°F, ≤0.19 @ 0°F, ≤0.18 @ +50°F, ≤0.19 @ +75°F, ≤0.23 @ +150°F, ≤0.26 @ +200°F mean; hot-surface C411 at 300°F deflection ≤0.25 in; water absorption C272 ≤2.0 % vol; WVP E96 ≤4.0 perm-in; dimensional stability D2126 ≤1 % (-40°F), ≤4 % (158°F/97% RH), ≤2 % (212°F); closed cell D6226 ≥90 %; service 300°F max / -297°F min.

Kingspan brochure pairs Type II with Tarecpir 2.5 (2.5 pcf min, '≥35' psi typical parallel) and Tarecpir HT/2.5 ('Type II HT †', -328°F to 350°F for the HT grade only); Kingspan sales sheets list Type II '30 PSI'. JM Trymer 2500 'ASTM C591, Grade 2, Type II'. Type-to-density pairing is from manufacturer literature, not the ASTM page.
Kingspan: Tarecpir 3.0, 3.0 pcf min, compressive '≥45' psi (brochure) / '45 PSI' (sales sheets).
Kingspan: Tarecpir 4.0, 4.0 pcf min, compressive '≥80' psi; 'Load-bearing insulation & pipe support inserts'.
Kingspan: Tarecpir 6.0, 6.0 pcf min, compressive '≥125' psi; 'Higher-load pipe support & concentrated load applications'.
ASTM abstract says grades are by service temperature range; Grade 1 range not public and not stated by NIA or either manufacturer.
NIA chart column 'C591 Grade 2': max 300°F, min -297°F (secondary). JM states 'Grade 2' for Trymer 2000XP; Kingspan states no grade.

spec_limits_per_nia_chart.note: Secondary source; values read from the rendered page image. NIA: 'This chart provides the reader with material properties as typically specified in ASTM material specifications ... may not be sufficient for writing specifications'; note 1 'All properties should be verified with individual manufacturers'; note 6 'Some values such as specific thermal conductivities at various mean temperatures may be interpolated or extrapolated by a small amount'. N/A = mean temperature outside the standard's scope; N/S = 'The ASTM standard makes no mention of this property'; N/R = no required performance for this classification. Ranges span the C591 types (densities 1.8–6.0). These are spec limits, not product values.

typical_applications.text: Below-ambient refrigeration piping (including ammonia), vessels, tanks and equipment, with a separate low-perm vapor retarder
Commercial chilled-water piping in non-plenum locations (JM: rooftop, mechanical room, pipe chases, industrial); plenums need a 25/50 product such as Trymer 25-50
Cryogenic service such as LNG and liquid oxygen (Kingspan Tarecpir 2.0 'Industries'; JM Trymer PIR family)

Above-ambient service up to 300°F: hot water, low-temperature steam (Kingspan) and the hot-gas portion of refrigeration systems (JM hot guide); composite system with a higher-temperature inner layer if 300°F is exceeded for more than brief periods
Load-bearing pipe supports, saddle and hanger inserts fabricated from higher-density PIR (JM Trymer 3000/4000/6000; Kingspan Tarecpir 4.0/6.0)
Industrial pipe insulation including elbows and fittings, tank and vessel insulation; also non-pipe panel cores and roof board (JM)

pros.text: Low k: 0.19 at 75°F mean for both products; falls to 0.13 (JM) / 0.11 (Kingspan, aged) at -200°F
One material spans -297°F to 300°F (C591 scope), from cryogenic to hot water

pros.text: Light (about 2 pcf) and closed-cell with low water absorption (<0.7 % JM; 0.47 % Kingspan)
Same chemistry in higher densities (to 6 pcf, ≥125 psi) for matching pipe-support inserts

cons.text: Combustible organic foam: E84 smoke ≤450 (JM, up to 4 in) or ≤250 (Kingspan, at 4 in), not 25/50, so not for plenums; no E136 noncombustible claim

cons.text: Not a vapor retarder (4 perm-in JM, 2.49 perm-in Kingspan); cold service needs a separate ≤0.02-perm vapor retarder and sealed joints (JM)
Degrades in sunlight and must be covered; chars above 300°F with higher k
Supplied as bunstock and fabricated to order: no published stock pipe-size or thickness tables; refrigeration work over 2-1/2 in thick must be double-layered (JM)
Blown-gas foams lose a little insulating value over time as air replaces cell gas

discrepancies_between_products: Maximum service temperature: JM Trymer 2000XP 08/10/26 sheet 350°F (176°C) vs Kingspan Tarecpir 2.0 300°F (149°C). ASTM C591-22 scope stops at 300°F.

JM internal: 08/10/26 sheet 350°F vs superseded 02/15/23 sheet, JM Trymer PIR page and Selector Guide IND-902 (01/19/26), all 300°F. The 08/10/26 sheet also keeps footnote (5), 'Above 300°F, discoloration and charring will occur', and the hot install guide (4/23/25) calls for a composite inner layer above 300°F. JM page gives 148°C for 300°F; data sheets give 149°C.

k at the same printed temperatures (JM 'Temperature (°F)' column, aging not stated, vs Kingspan C177 aged 6 months): -200°F 0.13 vs 0.11; -150°F 0.15 vs 0.13; -100°F 0.17 vs 0.16; -50°F 0.19 vs 0.18. Equal at 0°F (0.19), 50°F (0.18) and 75°F (0.19). Kingspan also publishes -265°F (0.07), 150°F (0.23) and 200°F (0.26); JM publishes nothing above 75°F.
Density: JM 2.05 pcf (Selector Guide '2.0 lb PCF') vs Kingspan 2.02 pcf.
Compressive (D1621): JM 25 psi parallel / 24 width / 30 length vs Kingspan 29.2 parallel / 18 width / 26.8 length.
Water vapor permeability (E96): JM 4 perm-in, at the C591 Type IV maximum of ≤4.0 as reproduced by Kingspan, vs Kingspan 2.49 perm-in.
E84: JM ≤25/≤450 up to 4 in vs Kingspan ≤25/≤250 at 4 in.
Closed-cell content: JM 90 % vs Kingspan 97 %. Water absorption (C272): JM <0.7 % vs Kingspan 0.47 % by volume.
C591 classification: JM 'Grade 2, Type IV' vs Kingspan 'Type IV' with no grade.

Kingspan internal: sales sheets give Type II (2.5 pcf) compressive '30 PSI' vs brochure '≥35'. Sales-sheet k maxima for Type III and Type V are '≤0.21' vs brochure 0.20 and 0.19. Sales sheets cite ASTM C165 for compressive and C177 for the '≤0.22' headline k; the data sheet and brochure use D1621 and C518. Brochure cites D2856 for closed-cell content; the data sheet uses D6226. The Tarecpir 2.0 C591 column shows 'Not specified' for C518 aged 75°F; the archived ISO-C1 page shows '≤0.19 (0.027)'.
Kingspan internal: at 0°F the sheet prints product 0.19 (0.028 W/m·K) against a C591 limit of ≤0.19 (0.027), so the SI value as printed exceeds the SI limit. The row is printed as '-0°F'.
Kingspan SDS internal: Section 2 says 'Combustible product.' while Section 9 says 'Flammability (solid, gas): Non flammable.'

JM internal: vapor retarder maximum permeance above 32°F is '0.030 perm' in the refrigeration guide (3.4.4) vs '0.30 perm' for service cycling above 32°F in the hot guide. The hot guide title reads '(60°F TO 297°F)', although the product limits are 300°F (or 350°F).

products[JM Trymer 2000XP].sizes – no stock IPS or copper size table and no wall-thickness range (fabricated from bunstock). The 36 in section length comes only from a general Trymer PIR brochure claim and the install guides' '36” direction'.

cons.text: Only 5 mm and 10 mm blanket thicknesses, so typical thicknesses need many layers (cut charts run to 12 layers; Cryogel vapor/banding schedule to 15), each with staggered seams; Pyrogel above 80 mm (3.2 in) needs Aspen Technical Services review

Cryogel Z cold systems still need a field-applied primary vapor barrier, a secondary foil-tape barrier below -40°F, vapor stops at every termination/penetration, and banding kept off the barrier layers

Neither product publishes a minimum service temperature, water-vapor permeability (perm-in), ASTM E136 result, pipe-apparatus (C335) k, or a roll length; current install manuals are form-gated (third-party copies used here)
Cryogel Z is limited to 257°F max; Cryogel Z E84 is ≤ 25/≤ 50 vs Pyrogel XTE ≤ 5/≤ 10

discrepancies_between_products: ASTM C1728 classification: Pyrogel XTE claims Type III, Grade 1A (product claim); Cryogel Z claims Type I, Grade 1B for the blanket it is 'produced from'.
Service temperature: Pyrogel XTE max 1200°F (650°C) vs Cryogel Z max 257°F (125°C); neither publishes a minimum. NIA spec-level ranges: Type III 75-1200°F, Type I -321-257°F.

k mean temperatures are not common: Pyrogel publishes at round °C means (32, 212, 392 ... 1112°F; no 75°F point), Cryogel at round °F means (-200, -100, 0, 75, 100, 200°F). Only the 200°F-vs-212°F region overlaps: Cryogel 0.13 at 200°F, Pyrogel 0.16 at 212°F.
Density (nominal): Pyrogel XTE 12.5 pcf vs Cryogel Z 10 pcf.
Compressive resistance minimum at 10% (C165, 2 psi preload): Pyrogel XTE ≥ 3 psi vs Cryogel Z ≥ 5 psi.
ASTM E84: Pyrogel XTE FSI ≤ 5 / SDI ≤ 10 vs Cryogel Z FSI ≤ 25 / SDI ≤ 50.
Vapor: Pyrogel XTE is 'Hydrophobic and breathable' (no vapor retarder) vs Cryogel Z laminated to a vapor retarder rated ≤0.00 perms (E96 dry cup).
Roll width: Pyrogel XTE 56-60 in (data sheet) / typically 60 in, up to 400 lb per roll (manual) vs Cryogel Z typically 57 in, up to 300 lb per roll (manual only).
Cut-chart convention: Pyrogel blanket cut charts 'Includes 1 in overlap'; Cryogel Z cut charts 'assume a butt joint with no overlap'.
Seam stagger: Cryogel Z manual specifies min 100 mm (4 in) stagger (12 in for PFP); the Pyrogel manual says only to overlap/stagger joints with no dimension.

Cryogel Z internal: the data sheet and product page describe an integral/integrated vapor retarder ('redundant protection'), yet the install manual still requires a separate primary vapor barrier (sheet mastic or mastic) over the outermost layer, plus a foil-tape secondary barrier below -40°F.

ASTM C1728 edition: the Pyrogel manual (v6.2, 2017) cites C1728-17; current is C1728-25a. The C1728-25a abstract mentions 'Types I, II, and III' while the NIA April 2024 chart tabulates Types I, III, IV and V.

cons.text: Brittle: JM says expanded perlite is 'a more brittle material than calcium silicate'
Water repellency is temperature-limited: JM says hydrophobic treatments burn off at 450°F; the material is not a vapor retarder (TPS: 'vapor permeable'; C610 states no permeability limit)
cons.basis: JM blog; TPS data sheet; NIA chart

cons.text: JM requires double-layer insulation at or above 600°F or over 3 in. thick, and metal jacketing outdoors, in corrosive areas and within 10 ft of the floor in mechanical rooms

Supply is thin and unsettled: the main brand's (JM Sproule WR-1200) product page and selector-guide entry are gone as of 2026-10-11; Howred's sheet is undated (2005 PDF); SMC and TPS publish k only as graphs
cons.basis: Observed on manufacturer sites and documents

discrepancies_between_products: Thermal conductivity at 200°F mean (ASTM C335 pipe): JM 0.481 vs Howred 0.48; at 700°F: JM 0.782 vs Howred 0.76. Howred's C177 values are higher than its C335 values (e.g. 200°F .53 vs .48). SMC and TPS give graphs only.

Section length: JM 36 in.; Howred 39.37 in. (1 m); TPS 24 in. ('Standard 2’ lengths'); SMC not stated. Per the Perlite Institute summary, C610-17 specifies 36 or 39.4 in.; TPS's 24 in. is outside that list although TPS says it 'Meets or Exceeds All Test Methods'.

Multi-layer: JM requires a double layer at ≥600°F or >3 in.; Howred advertises 'full rating without double layers' (1–4 in. single layer); SMC designs nested multi-layer pieces with no published threshold; TPS does not say.
Largest pipe size: JM quads to NPS 40 (curved block 30–126 in., lags above); Howred quads 22–24 in., curved radius block 20 in. and up; SMC quads 16–30 in.; TPS curved radius block to 60 in.
Compressive strength at 5%: JM >70 psi (data sheet) / 80 psi min (guide spec); Howred 134 psi average; SMC 90–110 psi; TPS >95 psi.
Density: JM '<15' pcf (C610 limit, no typical value); Howred 12 pcf nominal; SMC 12 pcf average; TPS '<14' pcf.
Linear shrinkage at 1200°F/24 h: JM <2%; Howred <1%; SMC <1.5%; TPS <1.0%.
Flexural strength: JM >45 psi; Howred 54 psi; SMC 80–105 psi; TPS >75 psi.
E84: JM, SMC and TPS publish 0/0; Howred publishes no E84 or E136 result.
Water behavior after heat: JM says hydrophobic treatments burn off at 450°F; TPS says EP-12 'Continues to resist water absorption even after a 600℉ (315℃) heat soak per ASTM C1763'.
Asbestos-free colour coding: JM blue; Howred pink; SMC gold; TPS green tint.
TPS's k graph legend reads 'ASTM C533 MAXIMUM' (the calcium silicate spec) although EP-12 is a C610 perlite.
Test-method labels: JM prints 'ASTM C442' for maximum service temperature (TPS prints C447); density method JM C302, SMC C303, TPS C302/C303.
JM internal: compressive >70 psi (data sheet IND-200 04/10/25) vs 80 psi minimum (guide spec IND-503 of the same date) vs 80 psi (2010 IIG sheet) and '> 80 psi' (2017 JM blog).
JM internal: three-piece sections at NPS 20–24 for 2–4 in. (data-sheet footnote) vs starting at NPS 16–20 depending on thickness (packaging sheet IND-P-5).
JM internal: flat block 1-1/2–4 in. thick, 12 in. wide (data sheet) vs 1-1/2–5 in. and 6 or 12 in. wide (packaging sheet).
JM internal: guide spec scope prints '120°F (-49°C)'; 120°F is +49°C.

JM vs its 2010 IIG predecessor sheet: k at 100°F 0.412 (C335, 2025) vs .47 (2010, methods not separated); pipe NPS 1/2–24 + quads to 40 (2025) vs 1/2–40 (2010); thickness 1–4 in. (2025) vs 1–5 in. (2010); density '<15' vs 13 pcf average; flexural >45 vs 50–60 psi.
unverified: Water vapor permeability (perm-in) for every product; ASTM C610 states no limit (NIA 'N/S'). TPS calls EP-12 'vapor permeable' without a value.
Minimum service temperature: no product data sheet publishes one (JM guide-spec scope says 120°F; C610 scope starts at 80°F).
k at 75°F mean for every product (JM and SMC print only 'R-Value 2.2 per inch @ 75°F'); k at 100°F for Howred.
products[SMC AU-1200].thermal_conductivity and products[TPS EP-12].thermal_conductivity: published as graphs only, no numeric values.
products[Howred GOODTEMP]: ASTM E84 and E136 results; compressive test method; jacketing guidance; current revision of the data sheet (undated, PDF 2005).
products[TPS EP-12]: thickness range and multi-layer guidance; products[SMC AU-1200]: section length.
Copper tube sizes: none published by any perlite product.
products[JM Sproule WR-1200].market_status: product page removed and absent from the 2025–2026 JM selector guides; no discontinuation notice found.

Exact ASTM C610-17(2023) requirement tables are paywalled; the limits recorded come from the NIA chart (2024) and Perlite Institute summary of C610-17 (2023). The 0.48 at 100°F maximum k comes from a 2013 Insulation Outlook article and was not confirmed against the current edition.

Residential work first; light commercial and light industrial projects (Armacell); residential and commercial (K-FLEX)
Buried lines above the water table (K-FLEX; conduit below the water table)
Large pipes and vessels with Tubolit sheets/rolls (Armacell)

pros.text: Very low water vapor permeability: 0.02 perm-in (Armacell, E96 Proc. A) and <0.05 (K-FLEX); K-FLEX says most indoor applications need no additional protection
Light (1.5-2.0 pcf), flexible, fiber-free and non-dusting; 6 ft semi-slit or self-seal tubes cut with a knife
ASTM E84 25/50 at the tube thicknesses sold (≤1 in Armacell; K-FLEX states 1 in and also 1-1/2 in)

cons.text: Low upper limit: 200°F maximum (C1427 scope and both products) - hot-water plumbing only, not steam or hot process
Thermoplastic: may drip, melt or draw away in fire tests; 25/50 rating limited to ≤1 in (Armacell) / ≤1-1/2 in (K-FLEX); no ASTM E136 claim
UV-sensitive: outdoor/rooftop runs must be painted (Armacell WB Finish) or coated/jacketed; K-FLEX warns of melting from concentrated reflected light
Small size range: tube walls only 3/8-1 in and IDs to 4 in IPS (Tubolit SS) / 4-1/2 in ID (K-FLEX); larger pipes need sheet or roll
Positioned for residential/light commercial work (Armacell); low-temperature use below 0°F needs Armacell technical review; K-FLEX says cold lines in high humidity may need extra vapor barrier
No compressive strength and no k values outside about 50-120°F mean are published

discrepancies_between_products: k mean temperatures differ: Armacell Tubolit publishes 50/75/100°F (0.265/0.270/0.280, declared '≤'); K-FLEX PE publishes 75/100/120°F (0.27/0.28/0.295). They agree at 75°F and 100°F.
Lower service limit: Tubolit -297°F (consult Armacell below 0°F) vs K-FLEX PE -200°F; both are below the ASTM C1427 scope minimum of -150°F.
Water vapor permeability: Tubolit 0.02 perm-inch (E96 Procedure A) vs K-FLEX PE '<0.05' (E96; no unit or procedure printed).
Density: Tubolit 1.5-2.0 pcf (ASTM D1667) vs K-FLEX PE 1.5 +/- 0.5 pcf nominal (ASTM D1622).
Water absorption: Tubolit 0.2% by volume (ASTM C1763 Procedure B) vs K-FLEX PE <0.20% by volume (ASTM C209).
E84 25/50 thickness limit: Tubolit up to and including 1 in vs K-FLEX PE 1-1/2 in (compliance list and table) - but K-FLEX's own p.1 text says 1 in and below.
Size range: Tubolit semi-slit ID 3/8-2-5/8 in, Tubolit SS to 4 in IPS ID; K-FLEX PE 3/8-4-1/2 in ID. Both 3/8-1 in wall, 6 ft lengths.
Color: Tubolit dark gray or white; K-FLEX PE black.

Vapor guidance: K-FLEX PE says most indoor applications need no additional protection (extra vapor barrier may be needed on cold systems in high humidity); Armacell's Tubolit sheet makes no vapor-retarder statement.
Fire classification: Tubolit UL 94 HBF (File E55798) vs K-FLEX PE UL 94 HF-1 (#E300774); K-FLEX also claims NFPA 90A/90B at 250°F.

Armacell edition drift: 2007 Self-Seal sheet k 0.25 @75°F, 180°F upper / -200°F lower limit, density 2 pcf (D1622), 0.0 perm-in; 2017 sheet k 0.265/0.270/0.275 at 50/75/90°F, -297 to 200°F, 0.02 perm-in dry cup; 2024 sheet k 0.265/0.270/0.280 at 50/75/100°F.
K-FLEX internal: R-value table prints 1-1/2 in wall values for three IDs although the published wall range ends at 1 in.

Secondary sources disagree on the C1427 linear-change limit: NIA chart '7% max (C 356)' vs K-FLEX 'Required' column '% change (2.0 max)' for linear shrinkage at 200°F (edition/grade not stated in either).
